title: The Fandom Effect: Sports Urbanism 2026
gist: Oxford Economics and Gensler's pre-World Cup survey of 5,858 people in 17 North American markets finds strong appetite for programming around stadium districts but barriers from ticket prices and safety.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics and Gensler surveyed 5,858 people in 17 North American markets as a pre-2026 FIFA World Cup baseline for sports-anchored mixed-use districts.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Baseline dataset for sports-district real estate and urban-revival thesis.

insights.claim: 64% of avid fans already use the areas around stadiums and 94% of those surveyed say they would use the surrounding area if their preferred programming were in place.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Latent demand for non-event-day programming supports mixed-use stadium district development.

insights.claim: 85% say ticket prices have become too expensive and 16% have avoided a venue over safety concerns, which deter frequent visits to these districts.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Pricing and safety are the constraints on visit frequency and district revenue.
